statement: How many integers $x$ satisfy the inequality $|2x - 3| \le x + 3$?

choices.misconception: I distributed the negative only to the $x$, so $-(x + 3)$ became $-x + 3$. That gave $-x + 3 \le 2x - 3$, so $x \ge 2$, and I counted $2$ through $6$.
I found $0 \le x \le 6$ but counted only $1$ through $6$, forgetting that $0$ is an integer.
I solved only $2x - 3 \le x + 3$ to get $x \le 6$, and for the lower end I only required the right side to be nonnegative, $x \ge -3$, so I counted $-3$ through $6$.

hints: An inequality $|A| \le B$ means $-B \le A \le B$. Here $B$ contains $x$, so keep it in both parts.
Write $-(x + 3) \le 2x - 3 \le x + 3$ and solve the left part and the right part separately.
The left part, $-x - 3 \le 2x - 3$, gives $x \ge 0$. The right part gives $x \le 6$. Count the integers from $0$ to $6$ inclusive.

solutions.reliable: The inequality $|2x - 3| \le x + 3$ is the same as $-(x + 3) \le 2x - 3 \le x + 3$. Left part: $-x - 3 \le 2x - 3$ gives $0 \le 3x$, so $x \ge 0$. Right part: $2x - 3 \le x + 3$ gives $x \le 6$. The integers with $0 \le x \le 6$ are $0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$, which is $7$ integers. Check the edges: $x = 0$ gives $3 \le 3$ and $x = 6$ gives $9 \le 9$, but $x = -1$ gives $5 \le 2$ and $x = 7$ gives $11 \le 10$, which both fail.
